Good afternoon. Welcome to our Museum of Ancient
History, and to my department — curiosities of the
good old, far-off twentieth century. The twentieth
century was often called the Era of the Book. In those
days, there were books about everything, from ant
eaters to Zulus. Books taught people how to, and when
to, and where to, and why to. They illustrated,
educated, punctuated, and even decorated. But the
strangest thing a book ever did was to save the Earth.

You are choosing a quotation to show that books in the Era of the Book did much more than instruct readers; which quotation best carries that point? (A) there were books about everything, from ant eaters to Zulus (B) Books taught people how to, and when to, and where to, and why to. (C) curiosities of the good old, far-off twentieth century (D) the strangest thing a book ever did was to save the Earth

answerScheme.modelAnswer: the strangest thing a book ever did was to save the Earth

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding a Book Exhibition Week in the library hall. Write an advertisement of about 100 words for the school notice board inviting students to visit it and telling them what to expect.

markingPoints.description: Content: promotes the Book Exhibition Week and gives its theme — books that changed the world and even protected the planet.
Format: a display advertisement with a short bold headline and a single paragraph of about 100 words, suited to a notice board.
Organisation: the ideas run in a clear order — the invitation, then what visitors will see and learn, then a closing appeal.
Accuracy: correct spelling, grammar and punctuation throughout, with no sentence left unfinished.
Expression: clear, lively language addressed to students your own age, using at least one concrete example from the exhibition.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
BOOK EXHIBITION WEEK
Students are invited to the library hall this week to meet the books that changed the world. Follow the strange case of the Martian invasion of 2040, which never really happened because a single book stopped it. Laugh as a Martian crew picks up a book of nursery rhymes, calls it a sandwich and takes orders to eat it. Discover why the twentieth century was called the Era of the Book, when there were books about everything and they taught people how to, when to, where to and why to. Come and decide for yourself. Entry free.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Trace in about 120 words, in clear steps, how the crew's guesses about the square place on Earth change, and how the order to eat the "sandwich" travels from Captain Omega to Sergeant Oop.

markingPoints.description: Step 1: Iota counts two thousand of the peculiar items and guesses the square place is some sort of storage barn.
Step 2: Oop, who has been to seven galaxies, opens a book, puts it on his head, guesses the items are hats and calls the place a haberdashery.
Step 3: Think-Tank reasons that since Earth creatures are always eating, the place is undoubtedly a crude refreshment stand.
Step 4: He declares the book a sandwich, made of two slices of what is called bread with a filling between them.
Step 5: Ordered to eat it to confirm his opinion, Omega refuses because Iota has not had her breakfast, and passes the order on to Iota.
Step 6: Iota will not eat before her Sergeant, so she hands the book to Oop and orders him to eat the sandwich immediately.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Iota counts two thousand of the peculiar items and guesses the square place is a storage barn.
2. Oop, who has been to seven galaxies, opens a book, puts it on his head, and guesses they are hats — a haberdashery.
3. Think-Tank reasons that since Earth creatures are always eating, the place is undoubtedly a crude refreshment stand.
4. He declares the book in Omega's hand a sandwich: two slices of bread with a filling between them.
5. He orders Omega to eat it, but she refuses, saying Iota has not had her breakfast, and orders Iota to eat it.
6. Iota will not eat before her Sergeant, so she hands the book to Oop and orders him to eat it at once.
